Title: 'Rechtwinklige Dreiecke' (right-angled spherical triangles). This page specializes the general spherical-trigonometry formulas of the previous page (8r) to the case of a right angle.

Diagram: a spherical triangle with vertices F, G and an unlabeled third vertex carrying the right angle (90°). The hypotenuse h joins F and G. The leg f runs from G to the right-angle vertex, so it is opposite F. The leg g runs from F to the right-angle vertex, so it is opposite G.

The six formulas, in modern notation (tang = tan):

I. cos h = cos f · cos g. This is the spherical Pythagorean theorem. [My derivation] Put A = 90° (so a = h) in the side cosine law cos a = cos b cos c + sin b sin c cos A.

II. cos h · tan F · tan G = 1, i.e. cos h = cot F cot G. [My derivation] Put the right angle into the angle cosine law cos A = −cos B cos C + sin B sin C cos a. With A = 90° this gives 0 = −cos F cos G + sin F sin G cos h.

III. sin h · sin F = sin f. [My derivation] Sine law: sin f / sin F = sin h / sin 90°.

IV. tan h · cos F = tan g, involving the leg adjacent to F. [My derivation] Use the four-part (cotangent) formula cos A cos c = cot b sin c − cot B sin A with the right angle as one of the angles. Equivalently, use the analogue formula sin a cos B = cos b sin c − sin b cos c cos A with A = 90°, which gives sin h cos F = cos f sin g. Divide by cos h = cos f cos g.

V. tan F · sin g = tan f, involving the leg opposite F and the leg adjacent to F. [My derivation] From the cotangent formula with the right angle: cot F sin g = cot f.

VI. sin F · cos g = cos G. [My derivation] Put the right angle into cos A = −cos B cos C + sin B sin C cos a, taking G as the left-hand angle: cos G = sin F cos g.

Together these are the six independent relations from which all ten Napier relations follow, using I–VI and their versions with F↔G, f↔g interchanged. Purpose: a reference sheet of formulas for solving right spherical triangles, e.g. in astronomy and geodesy.

results.what: Complete set of relations for right-angled spherical triangles: cos h = cos f cos g; cos h = cot F cot G; sin f = sin h sin F; tan g = tan h cos F; tan f = tan F sin g; cos G = sin F cos g
results.modern_name: Napier's rules (Napier's rules of circular parts) for right spherical triangles; spherical Pythagorean theorem
results.usually_credited_to: John Napier (Mirifici logarithmorum canonis descriptio, 1614); individual relations go back to medieval Islamic astronomers and Regiomontanus

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook formulas for right spherical triangles, written as a reference list following the general formulas on the previous page. Nothing non-standard.

III: sin h sin F = sin f (≈ 0)
IV: tan h cos F = tan g (≈ 0)
VI: sin F cos g = cos G (≈ 0)
II follows symbolically from I and V (and its f↔g analogue): result 0
